## What it is

The record of one report of a suspected incident or breach, from the first report through triage, notifications and closure, with a register of every report, as SP 800-53 IR-6 and IR-5 require.

## Controls satisfied

| Control | Title |
| --- | --- |
| [IR-6](/controls/ir/ir-6/) | Incident Reporting |
| [IR-6(1)](/controls/ir/ir-6/#ir-6.1) | Automated Reporting |
| [IR-5](/controls/ir/ir-5/) | Incident Monitoring |
| [IR-7](/controls/ir/ir-7/) | Incident Response Assistance |
| [IR-8(1)](/controls/ir/ir-8/#ir-8.1) | Breaches |

The register as a spreadsheet: [CSV](/downloads/forms/incident-report-form.csv), with one column per field.

## Preview (annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
This is the form IR-6(1)'s typical value names: anyone can submit Parts A to C, and the case management system alerts the incident response team when they do. The team completes Parts D to F, so one record shows when the incident was discovered, reported and declared, which is the first thing an assessor checks against the reporting time (IR-6a). Section 5.1 of the [incident handling playbook](/templates/procedures/incident-handling-playbook/) is the process this form records, and the [Incident Response Plan](/templates/plans/incident-response-plan/) sets the severity levels in Part D. Part C's questions come from the list [NIST SP 800-122](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/122/final) (April 2010), section 5.1, says is helpful to get from someone reporting a known or suspected breach involving personally identifiable information. Most organizations hold these fields in a web form that feeds the case management system rather than in a document; that is fine as long as each record has them. Keep the form short for reporters: Parts A to C should take a few minutes. The register at the end is also downloadable as a CSV file.
:::

| Report ID | Date and time received | Received through | Incident record ID | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### 1. How to use this form

- Anyone who suspects an incident or a breach completes Parts A to C, or calls the service desk, which completes them during the call. Report within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period for personnel to report suspected incidents to the organizational incident response capability <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 1 hour of discovery</span></span> (IR-6a). Do not wait to confirm it, and do not investigate first.
- Report what you know. A blank answer is better than a guess, and the team will follow up.
- Describe information that was exposed without copying it into the form: write "a spreadsheet of customer names and account numbers", not the names and numbers.
- Submitting the form through <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms used for reporting incidents <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the incident report form and case management system, which notify the incident response team automatically</span></span> alerts the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> (IR-6(1)).
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> completes Parts D to F and enters the report in the register.

| Field | Entry |

### Part B. What happened

| Field | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| Date and time it was discovered | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: date and time</span> |
| What you saw or what happened | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: description in your own words</span> |
| How it was noticed | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: for example a suspicious email, a security alert, a missing device, a customer's call</span> |
| Systems, devices or services involved | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: names, addresses or asset tags, and any connection to other systems</span> |
| Where it happened | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: office, remote, a supplier, a cloud service</span> |
| Is it still happening? | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes, no, or not sure</span> |
| What you have done so far | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: for example disconnected the laptop, forwarded the email to the service desk, nothing</span> |

### Part C. Information involved

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| What information was, or may have been, lost, exposed, changed or deleted? | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: a description, not the information itself</span> |
| Does it include personal information about people, such as names with identification numbers, financial, health or contact details? | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes, no, or not sure</span> |
| If yes: about how many people? | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: number or estimate</span> |
| What medium was it on? | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: for example laptop, phone, removable media, paper, a cloud service, email, a conversation</span> |
| Was it protected, for example encrypted or password protected? | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes, no, or not sure, and how</span> |
| Has anyone outside the organization been told, such as law enforcement or the recipient? | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: no; or yes, who and when</span> |

:::note[Guidance]
"Not sure" on personal information still sends the report to the privacy official: the incident handling playbook (5.2 step 3) brings them in whenever personally identifiable information is, or may be, involved. NIST's IR-2(3) discussion stresses reporting both confirmed and suspected breaches in any medium or form, including paper and oral, so the medium question lists both.
:::

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

Federal agencies notify the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) of incidents under FISMA (44 U.S.C. §§ 3553 and 3554). As of October 2026, the [CISA Federal Incident Notification Guidelines](https://www.cisa.gov/federal-incident-notification-guidelines) (effective April 1, 2017) require a report within one hour of identification by the agency's top-level incident response team, security operations center or IT department, with seven required elements. Part D's impact fields follow the guidelines' functional impact, information impact and recoverability categories, so the report can be filed from this form. CISA asks agencies not to include sensitive personally identifiable information in submissions.

[OMB Memorandum M-25-04](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/M-25-04-Fiscal-Year-2025-Guidance-on-Federal-Information-Security-and-Privacy-Management-Requirements.pdf) (January 15, 2025), the most recent FISMA guidance memorandum as of October 2026, section X, sets the major incident fields below. Events still unresolved after 72 hours of investigation are reported to CISA. A major incident determination is required for a breach affecting the personally identifiable information of 100,000 or more people. A major incident is reported to CISA and the OMB Office of the Federal Chief Information Officer within 1 hour of the determination, to the appropriate congressional committees and the Office of Inspector General within 7 days of the reasonable-basis determination, and, for a breach, in a supplemental report to Congress within 30 days of discovering it. [OMB Memorandum M-17-12](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/memoranda/2017/m-17-12_0.pdf), section VIII, requires the principal security operations center to track each breach, including the number of individuals, the types of information, whether individuals were notified or offered services, and whether it was reported to CISA or Congress.

| CISA element | Entry |
| --- | --- |

| Information impact (CISA category, for example privacy data breach) | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: one or more categories</span> |

| Number of systems, records and users affected | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: numbers or estimates</span> |
| Network location of the observed activity | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: location</span> |
| Point of contact | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: name and contact</span> |
| Attack vector, indicators of compromise and mitigation, if known | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: details</span> |

| CISA tracking number | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: number</span> |

| Reported to CISA and the OMB Office of the Federal Chief Information Officer | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: by whom, date and time, within 1 hour of the determination</span> |
